ranked.probe:
CANARY-PAINT + SINGLE-READER SIEVE. One harness, one word under test (WUT) per run, body loaded at I-RAM 0x6E (the slot the kernel already expects and the firmware never fills).

Grounding (checked in disasm/kernel.dsm, the 45/60 silicon-resident words): the kernel ITSELF executes ACT 0x0B three times (w26 `088012040B` class1 addr8 0x20 SRC 0x10; w46/w54 `080016000B` class1 addr8 0x60 SRC 0x00), ACT 0x17 once (w10 `0282A01417`), ACT 0x1A once (w41 `0400A0021A`). Three of the seven targets are already proven-executable words — the WUT is a REAL word, not a synthesised one. The anchored ALU model (instruction-set.md) says ACT writes **L**, the bus value, not acc: `lo12[4:0]: 13/19 -> tempA<-L, 14 -> tempB<-L, 07 -> mem[p]<-L`. Note 0x07 and 0x19 are ALSO the SRC codes for mem[p] and tempA ⇒ pre-registered hypothesis R1 (MIRROR): **ACT X writes the register SRC X reads**, and 0x13/0x14 are aliases. R1 predicts ACT 0x1A = tempB (aliasing 0x14) and ACT 0x0B = whatever SRC 0x0B reads.

Host setup (before RUN):
  POKE C-RAM[0xC0..0xC6] = P=0x600000 (poison), 0x400000, 0x200000, 0x100000, 0x080000, 0x040000, and G=gate coefficient.
  POKE D-RAM identity fill mem[a]=a over the probe's pointer window (so an address-register write self-reports, B6 trick).

Body (~34 words, every word a kernel shape with at most ONE 5-bit field substituted, marked <-):
  P0/P1  LOAD acc<-C-RAM[0x400000] (w30 shape) ; w10 with ACT<-0x13   => tempA = 0.50
  P2/P3  LOAD acc<-C-RAM[0x200000] ; ACT<-0x14                        => tempB = 0.25
  P4/P5  LOAD acc<-C-RAM[0x100000] ; w34 `0000AFF407` verbatim        => mem[p] = 0.125
  P6     LOAD acc<-C-RAM[0x600000]                                    => acc/L = P (poison)
  F0..F7 8x kernel no-op `0692200415` (ACT 0x15)                      (latency guard)
  WUT    `088012040B` with ACT<-X   [X = 0x0B baseline, or 0x1A/0x1B/0x1D/0x11/0x16/0x17]
  G0..G7 8x `0692200415`
  R0     READER = kernel w39 `0410AFF647` with SRC<-c, ACT 0x07  (mem[p_out] <- register c)
         c swept over {0x07,0x10,0x19,0x1A,0x00,0x08,0x0B,0x11, and X itself}
  E0/E1  MULTIPLY+EMIT: class-A multiply P=(C-RAM[G] x mem[p_out])>>6 (w5/w45 shape), then store to the output cell (w55 shape)

Phase 1  (destination): sweep reader c. The reader that no longer returns its painted canary, and instead returns P=0.75, names the destination.
Phase 1b (is it L or acc?): repeat with WUT's SRC<-0x19 (tempA) while acc still holds P. R1 predicts the destination receives 0.50 (tempA), not 0.75. Separates "ACT moves the bus L" from "ACT moves acc/the product".
Phase 1c (address registers): if no data register moved, re-read mem[p] and the cursor-fetched coefficient — against the identity fill, a changed pointer/cursor returns a DIFFERENT marker whose value IS the new address.
Phase 2  (route hypothesis R2, "ACT 0x0B = the all-pass core's 4th multiplicand route"): drop a proven `acc += P` word (f31=1, ACT 0x12) immediately after WUT and read acc. With each candidate multiplicand painted a distinct power of two, the accumulated product's RATIO to the null names the route.
Phase 3  (is the field an enum or a bitfield?): rerun Phase 1 on the one-bit neighbours of 0x0B — 0x0A, 0x09, 0x0F, 0x03, 0x1B. Shared behaviour along a bit answers the "0x12 and 0x15 both mean no action" anomaly structurally, independent of any single decode.
Latency calibration first: run the ACT<-0x13 positive control with filler counts {0,1,2,4,8,16}; the smallest count at which tempA reads P is the write->read latency (the known consumer-lag / "land <= 4" hazard). Use >= 2x it. If 16 fillers still fail, the harness is broken and NOTHING is reportable.
ranked.discriminates:
R1 MIRROR (ACT X writes the register SRC X reads) predicts: reader SRC=X returns the poison 0.75, every other reader returns its own canary unchanged. Sharp corollary, pre-registered: ACT 0x1A must land in tempB, i.e. be indistinguishable from ACT 0x14 — and the two must be tested in the same take.
R1' FLAT ENUM, unrelated destination predicts: some OTHER reader (not X) returns the poison. Same observable class, different row lights up — so R1 and R1' are separated by WHICH row, not by whether anything moves.
R2 MULTIPLICAND ROUTE (the standing class-A anchor for 0x0B) predicts: NO reader changes in Phase 1, but in Phase 2 the accumulated product differs from the null by exactly the ratio of two painted operands, and that ratio names the route. R1 and R2 make OPPOSITE Phase-1 predictions — this is the discriminating pair.
R3 NO-OP ALIAS (like 0x12/0x15) predicts: no reader changes AND Phase 2 matches the null. Indistinguishable from R2 in Phase 1 alone; Phase 2 is what separates them, which is why Phase 2 is not optional.
L-vs-acc: R1/R1' as stated (destination <- L) predict Phase 1b delivers 0.50; a "destination <- acc" or "destination <- product" reading predicts 0.75 or coef*0.75>>6. Same rows, different value — separated by amplitude, not by position.
Enum-vs-bitfield (Phase 3): an enum predicts the five one-bit neighbours of 0x0B behave independently; a bitfield predicts they cluster by bit. Nothing else in the project can ask this question.
ranked.negative:
A clean negative is: every reader returns its painted canary to within 0.5 dB, Phase 1b shows no change, Phase 1c shows no pointer/cursor movement, and Phase 2's product equals the null's. That reads "ACT X writes nothing we painted and routes nothing we varied" — i.e. X joins 0x12/0x15 as a no-action code, or its destination is outside the candidate set (which the identity fill and the enumerated reader list bound explicitly).
That negative is only reportable if, IN THE SAME RECORDING, the ACT<-0x13, ACT<-0x14 and ACT<-0x07 positive controls moved tempA, tempB and mem[p] to the poison. If the anchored codes do not light up, the instrument cannot see the failure and the negative is void — no exceptions.
The probe can also fail in a way that is not a result at all: the beacon (chop present at all) absent means the body at 0x6E never executed. Do not confuse that with "the word did nothing".
ranked.control:
Four, all in the same take at the same gain:
(1) NULL WORD — WUT slot filled with kernel word `0692200415` (ACT 0x15, a proven silicon no-op). Every reader must return its canary. If a canary moves here, the harness itself is contaminating registers and every reading is void.
(2) ZERO PAINT — all canaries poked to 0x000000. Every reader must return silence-level. Guards RULE 13 and the known "constant of the idle machine" trap (the 88 235 781 586 column): a reader that returns a fixed number regardless of paint is reading nothing.
(3) PAINT PERMUTATION — swap tempA's and tempB's canaries (0.50 <-> 0.25) and confirm the readback follows the paint, not the reader index. Kills the "the reader's SRC field is being ignored" failure mode.
(4) PRIMING CONTROL — repeat one configuration with a note held for >= 2.5 s (the NOTEOFS systematic: bodies read empty at note-on +1.0 s) and once with the input muted. The probe consumes no input operand, so the two must agree; disagreement means the body is not priming and every earlier reading is suspect.

commands: LOAD addr, words[] -- 1-word in-place patches of the resident kernel
RUN n
DUMP addr, len -- SPEC CHANGE: must reach CPU-2's memory-mapped I/O, not only RAM; this is the whole readout for Search 2
POKE space, addr, v -- SPEC CHANGE: add space 4 = CPU-2 address space, so 'RQ set' is just a poke to whatever latch the schematic names
RQ set -- only if step 0 locates the latch; otherwise subsumed by the extended POKE
GF read -- DROP IT from the monitor spec: it presupposes the answer Search 2 is looking for, and DUMP subsumes it
ranked.readback: TWO channels, one per search, neither of them the tone-generator-cell route. Search 1 (COND): AUDIO. RMS of the effect return over ten 50 ms windows with a sustained note held; the two states are wet-normal vs wet-silent, calibrated to >=40 dB separation before any sweep. RMS (not DC) so the analog path's AC coupling is irrelevant. Search 2 (GF): DIGITAL, but via DUMP of CPU-2's memory-mapped I/O diffed against a nop baseline -- explicitly NOT via a `GF read` command, because we do not yet know which port bit GF is. If the schematic (step 0) names the port, the diff collapses to a single-address read.
flaws: WRONG CPU — the instrument does not reach the DSP. The monitor is patched into qsigcwsa1ax.ic12 = CPU 1 (WSA1R-SYSEX-MONITOR-BUILD.md); the DSPs hang off CPU 2's ports (wsa1.cpp:728 'P7 (DSPD0-7); P5.3 = C/D', /CS on P5.4/P5.5/P2.7). CPU1<->CPU2 is only the IC24/IC25 octal-latch mailbox (wsa1.cpp:4114) speaking CPU-2's existing protocol. LOAD, POKE, RUN, 'POKE space 4' and DUMP-of-CPU-2-I/O are therefore NOT spec tweaks to a validated monitor — they are a SECOND monitor burned into ic28 (prom_c), unbuilt and unpriced. The design's 'effort: high' hides a whole second ROM project.

SEARCH 2 HAS NO READBACK PATH AT ALL. GF (if wired) lands on a TMP95C061 internal-I/O port of CPU 2. That area is not on any bus the mailbox exposes, so CPU-1's PEEK can never see it; 'DUMP must reach CPU-2's memory-mapped I/O' is a CPU-2 agent, not a spec change. Worse, a blind full-I/O-image DUMP has READ SIDE EFFECTS (UART RX data/status, timer status, EEPROM bit-bang lines on P6/P8, ATA task file) — reading the SC0 registers would eat the monitor's own SysEx stream. The readout can destroy itself.

THE DETECTOR IS BUILT ON A LIVE WORD, SO THE NULL IS NOT A NULL. kernel.dsm w46 = `0C00BC0407 ldreg r07,#iw94,0`, feeding w47 `00122011D5 mac (p),(p)+1`. BOTH K and N delete that register load. So N is not 'wet return NORMAL' — it is 'w47 stores through a stale pointer', itself a mutation. K and N differ only in acc-zeroing while sharing a corrupted pointer setup; the >=40 dB calibration will either fail or pass for the wrong reason (both variants scribbling on a random D-RAM cell). The whole Search-1 chain rests on this.

THE MAME NULL CONTROL CANNOT RUN THE HALF THAT MATTERS. wsa1r has no audio: all six wave mask ROMs are NO_DUMP (wsa1.cpp:4278-4294), the tonegen is a placeholder sine, and upd6383_device is a CPU device with NO sound_stream — its output never reaches a mixer. Control (1) (K-vs-N 40 dB calibration) and control (4) ('the entire battery must come out negative in MAME') are both impossible there. And MAME's negative is vacuous anyway: rq_w stores m_rq and nothing reads it (upd6383.h:250), so no hit is constructible — it tests the audio arm of the measurement chain not at all. RULE 12 ('no notes playing is not a test') cannot be satisfied in MAME either.

IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED THAT THE PATCHED CHIP IS AUDIBLE. The cited evidence is that the kernel is uploaded once at boot and that in-emulator C-RAM goes to IC6 (79 cells) / IC5 (54) with IC30 EMPTY. A chip holding zero coefficients may contribute nothing to the wet path. A failed calibration is then indistinguishable across five causes: wrong chip, wrong slot, wrong kill word, wet not isolated from dry, or COND absent. No positive control proves the audio instrument can see the failure before the sweep.
fixes: Re-scope step 0 and make it the ONLY thing attempted first, with a fourth outcome. Render the SX-WSA1R schematic AND trace (a) IC30 pins 83-88, (b) which CPU-2 port bits the latch sits on. Add outcome (d) 'schematic silent / no pin numbers' — the most likely result for a service manual — which returns UNKNOWN, not one of the three stated branches. Note the same question is already logged as open-for-Felipe in HARDWARE-CUSTOM-DSP-PROGRAMS-WSA1R.md; ask him to buzz the pins, which settles it faster than any probe.

Price the real blocker: a CPU-2 monitor in ic28. Until LOAD/POKE/RUN exist on the CPU that owns the DSP bus, both searches are unexecutable. Either build that monitor as its own milestone (with its own free-space/hook/RAM census, as ic12 needed), or find and document an existing CPU-2 mailbox command that already writes I-RAM — the bus scan says I-RAM is written ONLY at boot, so a runtime reload probably also needs the DSPRST/DSPRDY handshake and loses D-RAM delay state.

Move the probe word to a PROVEN NOP SLOT — w42, w45, w51, w54, w56 or w58 — and leave every live word intact, so N is a true null. Choose K so its store lands on a cell proven dead (or use a kill whose only effect is acc-zeroing). Then also confirm the chosen slot is inside the 45 runtime-resident words of the 63-word pool record; patching a non-resident slot yields a guaranteed flat result, i.e. a fake negative.

Add a POSITIVE AUDIO CONTROL before the sweep: prove the audio detector sees a change that MUST happen — upload an all-nop program, or assert DSPnRST2 — and confirm the wet path dies. Force 100 % wet on the effect mix; a dry-dominated send/return mix cannot show 40 dB. Normalise every RMS against the dry path or a fixed reference window, because 136+ reloads each require a re-struck note and note-to-note variance is the dominant noise against a 2 dB spread.

Widen Search 1's acceptance or it will reject real hits. A COND field plausibly encodes always/never and AND/OR of RQ bits, giving 1/7, 7/1, 2/6, 6/2 splits — all REJECTED by the stated 'clean 4/4 aligned to one RQ bit'. Accept any partition that is a consistent boolean function of RQ across 3 interleaved repeats, rank by simplicity, and keep the 4/4 case as 'strongest'. (The 6-of-254 arithmetic is correct for labelled assignments; the problem is narrowness, not the count.)

Distinguish COND from a board-level gate. A latch bit that also drives DSPnRST2, DSPCD or a mute produces the SAME 4/4 split as a COND hit, and control (2) only catches it when the side effect is audible with unmodified K/N. Add a cross-chip relocation (same word into IC5's or IC6's copy) and trace the latch bits on the schematic, not just pins 83-88.

Search 2: keep the audio detector LIVE as a batch canary instead of muting. As written, one wedged word silently voids the remaining 7 candidates of its batch across all ~448 — an undetectable false negative. Also test DC-STABILITY of any moved bit across repeated DUMPs BEFORE applying payload-identity: if the setter's payload comes from the accumulator or a data cell, GF toggles at 44.1 kHz, a single DUMP samples an arbitrary frame, and the 8/8 test rejects the genuine setter.
ranked.probe:
STEP 0 (do first, costs nothing, gates everything). Render the SX-WSA1R Service Manual effects-board schematic pages at >=300 dpi (/home/fsanches/compartilhado/KN7000/service_manual/SX-WSA1R Service Manual.pdf -- IMAGE-ONLY, grep returns nothing) and read IC30 pins 83-88. Three outcomes: (a) wired to a latch/port -> both searches armed AND the POKE/DUMP addresses are known, which deletes the blind port scan; (b) strapped to GND/VDD -> Search 1 runs degraded (fixed RQ), Search 2 dead; (c) NC -> whole axis dead on this board; report "unavailable on the WSA1R", NEVER "the chip has no COND field".

THE EXECUTION DETECTOR (shared by Search 1; built only from resident-kernel word forms). Take the 45-word resident kernel (wsa1/dsp/disasm/kernel.dsm) and substitute exactly ONE word, at slot 46 (currently `0C00BC0407`, a register load), immediately before the output store w47 `00122011D5` (mem[p]<-acc, acc=0):
  KILL word K = `00122FF1CE` (kernel w38's form verbatim, addr8 retargeted to a scratch D-RAM cell). Its documented effect is mem[p]<-acc, acc:=0. With acc zeroed, w47 stores 0 -> wet return SILENT.
  NULL word N = `0000200000` (kernel w42's nop, verbatim) -> wet return NORMAL.
Hold a sustained organ-type note throughout (RULE 12: a DSP test with no notes playing is not a test). CALIBRATE BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: measure RMS(N) and RMS(K) over ten 50 ms windows. Proceed only if RMS(N)/RMS(K) >= 40 dB with within-state spread <= 2 dB. If not, move the slot or swap detector shape; do not sweep a detector that cannot show its own two states.
NOTE the one confound already excluded by construction: hi12 bit 7 gates the STORE, and this detector reads the ACC-ZEROING, which bit 7 does not gate -- so bit 7 can be swept as a COND candidate without the store gate masquerading as a hit.

SEARCH 1 -- LOCATE COND. Candidate field, from the committed cross-corpus dark-codepoint census (dsp/tools/dark_codepoint_census.py): every one of the 36 bits is exercised in both corpora, so the target is a dark CODEPOINT, not a dark bit. Cross-validated dark: hi12[7:6]==3 (0/2989 KN5000, 0/4569 WSA1R) and class4 in {7,B,E,F} (empty in both). hi12 bit 0 is rare-but-live (15/2989, 27/4569). The KN5000-only reading "hi12[6:5]==3 is dark" does NOT survive the WSA1R (14 words) -- it was dropped.
  Variant set: K with all 64 combinations of hi12 bits {9,8,7,6,5,0} (bits 9/8 are the proven-but-unmeaning f98 field), plus K with class4 replaced by each of {7,B,E,F}. 68 variants.
  Stage A (coarse, ~1 min): each variant at RQ=0 and RQ=7 only, 136 LOAD+RQ+RUN+measure cycles. Only variants whose two readings differ by >20 dB advance.
  Stage B (confirm): survivors swept over all 8 RQ values, 3 interleaved repeats in Gray-code order (interleaving is mandatory -- note decay and thermal drift are slow and would otherwise imitate an RQ dependence).
  ACCEPTANCE, all three: (i) the 8 RQ readings split into two groups >=20 dB apart; (ii) within-group spread <= 2 dB; (iii) the split is one of exactly 6 admissible partitions -- a clean 4/4 aligned to RQ bit i or its complement. 6 of 254 possible partitions, so this is not a criterion anything can pass by accident.
  RELOCATION CHECK: move the winning word to a different I-RAM slot with a different scratch cell. The RQ->execute relation must follow the WORD, not the slot.

SEARCH 2 -- LOCATE THE GF SETTER. Do NOT use a `GF read` command: it presupposes knowing where GF is. Instead scan. For each candidate word W: LOAD kernel-with-W-at-one-slot, RUN, DUMP CPU-2's whole memory-mapped I/O image, diff against a nop-substituted baseline. Because the PC restarts every frame at 44.1 kHz, a GF-setting word fires ~44100x/s and GF is statically set -- no timing needed, a single DUMP suffices.
  Candidate families, ordered: F1 the ESC register-write form (kernel w57 shape `08190868SS`, selector lo12[7:0]=SS swept 0x00-0xFF, payload addr8=0x07) = 256; F2 the four cross-dark classes {7,B,E,F} with lo12 ACT swept 0x00-0x1F = 128; F3 C-format opcodes [35:25] swept 0x600-0x63F (the neighbourhood of the 8 observed) = 64. ~448 total, batched 8 per program with bisection on a hit: ~56 runs plus 3 per hit.
  ACCEPTANCE, all three: (i) PAYLOAD IDENTITY -- sweep the payload 0..7 and the suspect bits must reproduce all 8 patterns, 8/8; (ii) REMOVAL -- W -> nop restores the reset value; (iii) RELOCATION -- same W at another slot, same bits. A bit that merely moves and fails (i) is some other side effect, not GF. Search 2 needs no audio; mute the return while scanning.

HAZARD, non-negotiable: arbitrary words can wedge IC30 or rail the output. Keep the stock kernel re-uploadable, mute during Search 2, and never blind-poke CPU-2 output latches the schematic has not identified (flash control and amp mute live there).
ranked.discriminates:
Three candidate readings of the situation, and they predict different things.
(R1) "COND exists, is in the undecoded hi12 bits or a dark class, and RQ is wired." Predicts: exactly one variant in Search 1 shows a clean 4/4 RQ-bit-aligned split, >=20 dB, which follows the word under relocation. Nothing else in the 68 does.
(R2) "COND exists but RQ is strapped to a fixed level on this board." Predicts: NO variant shows RQ dependence (Search 1 looks identical to a total negative), BUT one or more variants flip the detector state relative to plain K at the fixed strap -- i.e. a word that should kill the audio does not, or vice versa. R1 and R2 are distinguished by whether the effect tracks the host's RQ writes, and cross-checked by step 0's schematic read. R2's result is a CANDIDATE COND field that is unconfirmable without a hardware strap change -- label it that way, do not promote it.
(R3) "The pins are not brought out on this board at all." Predicts BOTH searches negative AND step 0 shows NC/strap. This is the only reading under which the negative is about the board rather than the ISA, and it is the reading step 0 settles for free.
For Search 2 the discrimination is sharper: any candidate producing a port-bit change is either the GF setter (passes payload-identity 8/8) or an unrelated side effect (fails it). Those two predict opposite outcomes on a sweep that costs 8 extra runs, so there is no ambiguous middle.
DIRECT decode yield is small and I will not inflate it: if COND lands on the dark codepoint hi12[7:6]==3 it renames ZERO corpus words (that is what "dark" means); if it lands on hi12 bit 0 it decodes 15 KN5000 / 27 WSA1R words; a GF setter in family F1 would name a handful of singleton hi12 values (819, 859, 82E, E30 and the C-format one-offs), ~8. The axis is worth running for the INSTRUMENT, not the word count: a 3-bit digital readout plus host-controlled conditional execution turns each remaining open question (37 hi12 + 36 lo12 values with no meaning, classes 3-8 uncharacterised, the output-stage null) from a multi-hour audio session into a ~1-minute binary question.
ranked.negative:
Search 1 NEGATIVE: all 68 variants read flat across RQ within the calibration's 2 dB spread, while the K-vs-N calibration proves the detector separates its two states by >=40 dB. That is a real, reachable outcome and it is informative: it excludes COND from hi12 bits {9,8,7,6,5,0} and from classes {7,B,E,F} -- a bounded exclusion, not an exhaustive one over 36 bits, and it must be reported as such.
Search 2 NEGATIVE: no port bit outside the nop-baseline's known-noisy set (timers, MIDI status, ADC) moves for any of the ~448 candidates, while the instrument-validation poke proves DUMP-diff can see a deliberate single-bit change. Conclusion: GF is not wired to CPU-2 on the WSA1R, or the setter lies outside F1-F3.
Step 0 NEGATIVE: pins 83-88 go to GND/VDD/NC -> the axis is unavailable on this board and the report says exactly that.
The failure mode that would VOID a result rather than produce one: the RQ control sweep (below) coming out non-flat, or the calibration failing to separate K from N. Both are checked before any hit is believed.
ranked.control:
FOUR controls, all mandatory.
(1) INSTRUMENT CALIBRATION: K-vs-N at slot 46 must separate >=40 dB with <=2 dB within-state spread. No sweep runs until it does. This is "prove the instrument can see the failure before reporting its absence".
(2) NULL FOR SEARCH 1: the full 8-value RQ sweep run against unmodified K and against N. Both MUST be flat. If either tracks RQ, the extended POKE is writing something other than the RQ latch and every Search-1 result is void.
(3) NULL FOR SEARCH 2: the nop-substituted program's DUMP-diff establishes the known-noisy bit set; plus a monitor-driven poke to one schematic-identified harmless output latch (a panel LED) that DUMP-diff must catch, proving the diff is not blind.
(4) MACHINE-LEVEL CONTROL, and the strongest one: MAME models GF and RQ as storage wired to nothing (upd6383.h ~line 245: "Neither the COND field nor the instructions that touch GF have been located"). So THE ENTIRE BATTERY MUST COME OUT NEGATIVE IN MAME. Run it there first: it debugs the monitor protocol for free, and any positive in MAME proves the measurement chain manufactures hits. MAME is the guaranteed-negative null machine for this axis.

commands: LOAD (I-RAM write: the 60-word header + 23-word epilogue stay resident, the body and the two setvec call-vector words are rewritten; one 5-byte word per variant)
POKE (C-RAM tag 0x26 for c[0..4]; D-RAM/register tag 0x15 for the operand cells 0x10/0x11/0x12 and the ramp cells 0x14/0x15)
RUN (delimits the capture window only - the probe is free-running and does NOT need frame-exact stopping)
RQ (Phase 3 only: host-write RQ1-3 to test whether f31 carries a condition)
DUMP (optional, CPU-2 RAM echo of the packet actually framed - upload hygiene, not a DSP readback)
ranked.readback: AUDIO OUTPUT, as the FREQUENCY of a sawtooth - not as a DC level. V (the result of the word under test) is scaled by c[2] and integrated into a 24-bit D-RAM cell once per frame, so the line out carries a sawtooth at f_T = 44100 * c[2] * V / 2^24, wrapping cleanly mod 2^24. Sign of V shows as the slope direction in the recorded waveform. c[2] is chosen so |V| = full scale gives ~2000 Hz, i.e. the 16 candidate answers of row R1 sit ~125 Hz apart - a 3% frequency measurement separates them, and a 30 s cycle count gives ~1e-5 relative (13-17 bits of V). A second sawtooth (the HEARTBEAT) at exactly 300.000 Hz, driven only by anchored words, is summed into the same output: it is both the liveness proof and the clock reference, so f_T/f_H is immune to the recorder's sample-clock error. This survives the AC-coupled line out, which a DC level would not. GF1-3 are NOT used anywhere - the design deliberately depends on nothing unproven. Option (c), a tone-generator-visible cell, is unavailable: the DSP sits downstream of the TG and nothing in its address space is CPU-readable.
flaws: THE SUCCESS CASE IS THE STATUS QUO. instruction-set.md's ADOPTED ALU already reads f31 as: SRC_TERM=0 iff f31==0, P_TERM=0 iff f31==2, else acc+P. So 1,3,4,5,6,7 ALL execute as ADD today. The design's outcome #2 ('3..7 alias ADD, that closes all 189 words') is what the running core already does - it decodes nothing, it re-confirms the default. The only informative outcome is a DISAGREEMENT, and the 19-candidate table (AND/OR/XOR/NEG/SHL1/ABS...) is an ISA fantasy with no corpus or datasheet support.

L IS NOT AN INPUT IN THE CHOSEN ENCODING, so R4 cannot fail. b4 carries ACT = lo12[4:0] = 0x15, not 0x00. The adopted model selects SRC_TERM = L ONLY when ACT == 0x00; otherwise SRC_TERM = acc. Six candidates (LOAD L, acc+P+L, acc-L, L+P, and the bitwise ones against L) are unreachable by construction and every k predicts the same answer in R4 - the project's own 'a criterion that cannot fail' trap.

R4's OPERAND IS NEVER READ. b2 is (p)+1 (0x10 -> 0x11); b3 and b4 are +0. The pointer never reaches 0x12, so C=0x0F0F0F is poked into a cell the probe never touches. And L at b4 = mem[0x11] = the SAME cell that forms P, so L and P are collinear by construction. Every R1 prediction that uses L (0F0F0F, 979797, 464646, 424242) is arithmetically wrong for the program as written.

b1 IS NOT AN INSTRUCTION - it is a host packet. `000.1.NN.000` is PROVEN BY CONSTRUCTION as the uC-IF 5-byte ADDRESS packet emitted by LABEL_03846C/038539/038CF9 ahead of a tag-0x15 value packet. Census: 0 occurrences in 8003 corpus microwords (dsp/tools/f31_context_census.py). The only attested in-program pointer loads are 801.0.NN.821 (C-RAM pointer) and 801.0.NN.825 (descriptor pointer) - NEITHER sets the D-RAM data pointer p. The probe has no attested way to place p on a chosen cell and never establishes p at body entry.

CONTEXT TRANSFER: the probe speaks for 9 of 235 words, not 189. Pooled census (committed, dsp/tools/f31_context_census.py): f31>=3 = 235 occurrences / 59 distinct. The probe's exact context (class 2, bit4=0, bit7=0, SRC 0x07) = 9 (3.8%). The DOMINANT shape is class 2, addr8 0x00, lo12 = 0x000 - SRC 0x00 AND ACT 0x00, 106 occurrences - which is a DIFFERENT adder configuration (SRC_TERM = L). Measuring f31 at SRC 0x07 / ACT 0x15 and claiming it for those 106 is the same unvalidated-site instantiation that killed the §135/§139 leads.

37 OF THE 235 CARRY THE STORE BIT (18 of them with bit7=1) and the store gate is FORCED to read bit7 AND hi12[3:1] - i.e. f31 itself. The design proudly sets bit4=bit7=0 to stay out of that, which means it cannot resolve those words at all. They are inside the 189 being claimed.

THE ONE-SLOT PIPELINE probably makes b5 read acc BEFORE b4 wrote it. The project's own bit-exact LLE is `P=(coef[N-1] x L[N])>>6, acc one-slot, operand L=mem[N-1]`. If the acc read is one-slot delayed, b5's L=acc is the pre-b4 accumulator, V never leaves the accumulator, all three anchors read alike and the run aborts at gate 1. Fail-safe, yes - but it is the MOST LIKELY outcome and no spacer words are budgeted.

THE ANCHORS DO NOT CANCEL THE SCALE, so the bitwise candidates are unreadable. You measure kA, kP, k(A+P); the third is the sum of the first two for ANY k, so k is not identified. Ratios suffice for the linear candidates only. AND/OR/XOR/ANDNOT need the ABSOLUTE bit patterns of A and P, and A = (c[0] x mem)>>s with s (>>6 / PSHIFT) unproven. 'One poke->measure->correct iteration lands A and P on the intended bit patterns exactly' is impossible from frequency ratios; Phase 0c calibrates the integrator, which is DOWNSTREAM of the multiply.

PHASE 3 CANNOT FAIL. RQ1-3 sits on the same unproven pin block (83-88) as GF; the board wiring is unknown for both. If RQ is not wired, every k is invariant under RQ - which is exactly the 'f31 is not a COND field' reading. No positive control for RQ exists anywhere in the project. The design's claim that it 'deliberately depends on nothing unproven' is false: it drops GF and then uses RQ.

AUTHORISATION AND CONSTRAINT CONFLICT. Standing decision, Felipe, 2026-09-14 (memory wsa1r-hardware-access-and-rom-sockets): DO NOT IMPLEMENT THE CUSTOM ROM CODE - the SysEx monitor is a design record only. LOAD (host upload of a synthesised I-RAM body) is precisely the parked item. Same testimony: no audio input, no digital output, analogue out + MIDI only, and 'measurements must be PARAMETRIC, never bit-exact' - against which a 13-17-bit readback of V is out of bounds.

NO HALT, SO EVERY UPLOAD IS A LIVE PATCH. 80 words over MIDI SysEx is ~0.25 s = ~11 000 frames of a half-built program executing into the output, writing garbage into the delay D-RAM the next variant inherits. No mute, no settle time, no inter-variant D-RAM clear is specified; run-to-run independence (control (d)) is assumed, not enforced.

NITS THAT BITE: 300.000 Hz is not representable (2^24 x 300/44100 = 114130.7), so the 'clock reference' is itself off by 6e-6 and drifts the ratio; and |delta| > 2^23 folds, making V and (2^24 - V) produce the same magnitude spectrum, so the sign claim rests entirely on slope visibility in a naive aliased saw.
fixes: Put the REAL corpus words under test, one shape at a time: 0026200000 (37), 002A200000 (30), 0028200000 (17), 002E200000 (11) - class 2, addr8 0x00, lo12 0x000, together 106 of 235 occurrences. A synthesised shape that occurs 9 times speaks for 9 words.

Because those carry ACT 0x00, run a 2-column matrix: ACT 0x00 (model says SRC_TERM = L) vs ACT 0x15 (model says SRC_TERM = acc), at every k. THAT is the design's real discriminator - the adopted model predicts f31 does not influence the L/acc selection, and a difference refutes it. It is also the only row in the design that could overturn a published reading.

Fix the operand plumbing or drop the L rows: choose addr8 so p visits three distinct cells, and recompute the R1 table for L = mem[p-as-actually-left], not for a cell the pointer never reaches. As written, L and P are collinear.

Delete b1. Do not assume absolute D-RAM addressing exists from inside a body - it is not an attested instruction. Instead sweep b4's addr8 over +/-N and find where the answer moves; that ALSO measures p at body entry, which nothing in the project currently knows, and is a cheap result in its own right.

Insert 2-3 anchored spacer words between b4 and b5 and make the spacing a MEASURED parameter (re-run the anchor gate at spacing 0/1/2/3). Otherwise the documented one-slot acc pipeline eats V and the whole campaign aborts at gate 1 with nothing learned.

Add an absolute-calibration leg: fix c[0] to a known value, sweep mem[0x10] over powers of two, measure f_0, solve the product shift s. Without it, DELETE AND/OR/XOR/ANDNOT from the candidate table and say in the design that bitwise readings are out of reach.

Kill Phase 3, or first find the ROM/board write that actually drives RQ. A test whose negative is indistinguishable from 'the wire is absent' has no power; the RQ question needs its own positive control before it is worth a single run.
Make the heartbeat increment dyadic (2^24/128 = 131072 -> 344.53125 Hz exactly) and bound |delta| < 2^22 by construction so no fold/alias ambiguity can arise.
Budget the 37 store-bit words (18 at bit7=1) as a SEPARATE probe at bit4=1 - they cannot be reached with the store suppressed, and until that exists stop counting them in the headline.
Get the 2026-09-14 standing decision lifted before scheduling any of this. Until Felipe says otherwise this is a design record, and any I-RAM-upload monitor command is unauthorised work.

ranked.probe:
GOAL: make the word under test a pure function g(acc, P, L) of THREE host-chosen constants, with no audio input anywhere, and read g back as a frequency.

KEY MOVE — do not trust the poked constants, trust the anchors. A := whatever the f31=2 (HOLD) run reads back. P := whatever the f31=0 (LOAD) run reads back. Every prediction for k=3..7 is expressed in the MEASURED A and P, so the unknown product scaling ((coef x L)>>6, PSHIFT), the Q0.23 coefficient range and the one-slot pipeline (L = mem[N-1], P from word N-1) all cancel. One poke->measure->correct iteration lands A and P on the intended bit patterns exactly.

PHASE 0 — gates. Each can fail; each aborts the run.
0a. LOAD a known-good body image (e.g. prog01_chorus) at I-RAM 84 and set the unit-0 call vector (the two host-written setvec words, KN5000 I-RAM 78/79). If the sound does not change, IC30 does not accept uC-IF cmd-01 outside boot -> STOP.
0b. PRESENTATION HUNT. Load a 6-word sawtooth generator built only from anchored words, writing its state to candidate cell q; sweep q over {acc-live-at-body-exit, 0x06, 0x0B, 0x50, 0x8C, 0x8D, 0x8F, ENTRY+0..+12} (unit-0 ENTRY = 0x05). The run that produces an audible sawtooth NAMES the presentation route. If none does -> no readback exists from a host-loaded body -> STOP.
0c. RAMP CALIBRATION. Poke the increment I over 4 decades; confirm f_out = 44100*I/2^24 is linear. Fixes the readback scale and proves the capture chain can see it.

PHASE 1 — the probe body at I-RAM 84. Only ONE word ever changes.
  b0  801.0.00.021   rstcur                      ; cursor -> unit-0 base (VERIFIED word, kernel w58)
  b1  000.1.10.000   ldptr.d #$10                ; D-RAM pointer -> 0x10 (PROVEN-BY-CONSTRUCTION family)
  b2  000.A.01.1D5   ld  (p),c+,(p)+1            ; f31=0 LOAD: acc <- c[0]*mem[0x10]  == A   (corpus 0000A001D5, 53 sites)
  b3  204.A.00.1D5   post (p),c+,(p)+0           ; f31=2 HOLD: acc untouched; P := c[1]*mem[0x11] == P
                                                 ;   (hi12 0x204 attested as 0204A061D5; 0104A001D5 = same f31, 15 sites)
  b4  *** THE ONE WORD UNDER TEST ***  hh.2.00.1D5
        class 2 = mode 2, NO cursor fetch -> the word does NOT re-multiply, so it consumes b3's product unchanged.
        Its three visible inputs: acc = A, P = b3's product, L = mem[0x11] = C (SRC 0x1D5>>6 = 0x07 = mem[p]).
        hh = BASE | (k<<1), BASE in {0x000, 0x200} (the f98 control), k = 0..7.
        bit4 = 0 and bit7 = 0 in EVERY variant, so the disputed store gate is out of the picture entirely.
        Corpus-attested siblings of this exact shape: 00002001D5 (30 sites, k=0) and the 0202/0212 class-2 family.
  b5  000.A.00.415   ld acc,c+,(p)+0             ; acc <- c[2]*acc  (corpus 0000A00415, 76 sites) - scales V into range
  b6  000.1.14.000   ldptr.d #$14                ; -> RT, the test ramp cell
  b7  202.A.00.1D5   mac (p),c+,(p)+0            ; acc <- acc + c[3]*mem[RT], c[3]=1 (corpus, 134 sites)
  b8  012.2.00.1CE   mac (p),(p)-1 ; mem[p]<-acc ; RT <- RT + c[2]*V, acc cleared (kernel w3 shape)
  b9..b12   HEARTBEAT: RH <- RH + c[4], same anchored shapes, c[4] poked for exactly 300.000 Hz
  b13..b15  present (RT + RH) at the cell found in 0b
  b16..b79  OPTIONAL x64 residual amplifier: 64 cascaded anchored ADD words, used only for rows whose coarse answer leaves a sub-0.01%-FS question.
Per variant the host sends ONE 5-byte LOAD at I-RAM 88. Nothing else moves.

PHASE 2 — operand matrix (POKE D-RAM 0x10=A, 0x11=B->P, 0x12=C; POKE C-RAM 0x00..0x04 = c[0..4]).
  R1  A=555555 P=333333 C=0F0F0F   main separator (all 19 candidates land on distinct 1/16-FS steps)
  R2  A=000000 P=333333 C=0F0F0F   is acc consumed at all? isolates the P-only part and any shift of P
  R3  A=333333 P=000000 C=0F0F0F   is P consumed? exposes unary ops (NEG / SHL1 / SHR1 / ABS)
  R4  A=555555 P=333333 C=000000   is L consumed? the three-input sensitivity test (one input at a time)
  R5  A=7FFFFF P=7FFFFF C=000000   overflow: wrap vs saturate vs averaging adder vs guard-bit growth
  R6  A=FFFFFF P=000001 C=000000   sign/borrow behaviour
  Each row: 8 k x 2 BASE = 16 runs x 3 s capture. 96 runs total, plus repeats.
PHASE 3 — RQ dependence. Repeat R1 and R3 with RQ=000 then RQ=111. If any k's value moves, f31 is (partly) the never-located COND field, not an arithmetic selector. Cheap, and a bigger prize than the arithmetic.
ranked.discriminates:
Predictions for R1 (A=555555, P=333333, C=0F0F0F), expressed in the MEASURED A and P, 24-bit:
  LOAD acc<-P        333333    ADD acc+P          888888    HOLD acc           555555
  SUB acc-P          222222    RSUB P-acc         DDDDDD    AND                111111
  OR                 777777    XOR                666666    ANDNOT acc&~P      444444
  AVG (acc+P)/2      444444    NEG acc            AAAAAB    SHL1 acc           AAAAAA
  SHR1 acc (arith)   2AAAAA    L+P (bus replaces acc) 424242 LOAD L             0F0F0F
  acc+P+L            979797    acc-L              464646    acc+(P>>1)         6EEEEE
  acc+(P<<1)         BBBBBB
Every one of these is a distinct 1/16-FS step except ANDNOT vs AVG, and R3 (P=0) splits those: ANDNOT->555555 (wait: R3 A=333333) ANDNOT->333333, AVG->199999. NEG vs SHL1 differ by 1 LSB in R1 and by 0x666666 in R3 (NEG->CCCCCD, SHL1->666666), so the coarse readback suffices.
Row logic: R2 (A=0) says whether acc is an input at all and exposes any shift applied to P; R3 (P=0) says whether P is an input and exposes unary acc ops; R4 (C=0) is the decisive test for the possibility nobody has tested - that f31 3..7 route the BUS operand L into the accumulator instead of acc (SRC_TERM selection), which would make them the missing input-route ALU; R5 separates a wrapping adder from a saturating one from an averaging one and shows whether the accumulator's guard bits are visible at the output; R6 pins sign/borrow.
Two candidates that predict the SAME thing everywhere, and I say so: OR and ADD are identical on any operand pair with disjoint bit patterns, which is exactly why R1 uses 555555/333333 (overlapping) - on disjoint operands the whole design is blind. Likewise HOLD and ANDNOT-with-P=0 and OR-with-P=0 all predict A in R3; only R1 separates them. And if two of 3..7 turn out to predict the same value on all six rows, the honest report is "these two values are indistinguishable on an accumulator probe", not "they are the same instruction".
Phase 3 adds an orthogonal discrimination: an arithmetic reading predicts NO change under RQ; a condition-field reading predicts that some k's result switches between its normal value and the HOLD value when RQ flips.
ranked.negative:
Four distinct negatives, all reportable:
1. GATE FAILURE (nothing about 3..7 is reported). Within every row, the k=0 run must read P, the k=2 run must read A, and the k=1 run must read A+P to within the readback error. If ADD != LOAD + HOLD, the setup does not deliver the operands I think it delivers - pipeline alignment, cursor position, or the product scaling is wrong - and the rig is declared unproven. This is the criterion that can fail and it is checked before any 3..7 number is looked at.
2. ALIASING. If f31=k reads identically to f31=1 on all six rows and under both f98 bases, the finding is "hi12 bits 2 and 3 are don't-cares in the accumulator path; 3..7 alias ADD". That closes all 189 words and is a real result, not a failure.
3. NOT AN ACCUMULATOR FUNCTION. If V is constant across R1..R6 (insensitive to A, P and C), the field does not feed the accumulator adder at all. If the TEST sawtooth goes to DC while the HEARTBEAT keeps running, V = 0 exactly (AND-like, or the word writes nothing). If the heartbeat ALSO stops, that k halts or traps the sequencer - it is a control op, which is also a decode.
4. OFF THE CANDIDATE LIST. If the six measured values for some k fit none of the 19 candidates, the report is the measured table plus "unresolved", and the follow-up is a linearity sweep (step P over 16 values at fixed A) to test whether g is affine in P at all.
ranked.control:
Five, and they run WITH the test, not after it (the per-category-control rule from the 2026-09-14 handover):
(a) ANCHOR CONTROL - k = 0/1/2 measured in every row; must reproduce LOAD/ADD/HOLD exactly. This is the calibration AND the proof the instrument can see the answer.
(b) HEARTBEAT - a 300.000 Hz sawtooth driven only by anchored words, summed into the same output. Separates "V = 0" from "the chip stopped", which is precisely the difference-from-silence trap (RULE 13).
(c) ZERO-OPERAND NULL - a full 8-k sweep with A = P = C = 0. Every k must show heartbeat only and no test tone. Any test tone here is a contaminated datapath and voids the row.
(d) REPEAT CONTROL - each row's k=1 run is re-uploaded byte-identically and re-captured, bounding run-to-run variance (it should be zero: the probe is deterministic).
(e) f98 CONTROL - the whole matrix at BASE 0x000 and BASE 0x200. If an unrelated hi12 field moves the answer, the single-axis framing is wrong and the result is withheld.
Plus the standing instrument control: the identical matrix run against the MAME LLE core, whose f31 3..7 currently trap. Agreement there proves only that the model matches itself - it is a rig shakedown, explicitly NOT evidence about the chip.
